notes: This runner has an end. The prompt says about thirty seconds of running reaches Andy, so winner-zone is emitted at the end of the chunk queue even though the genre is defined by an endless path. The chunk rules still apply up to that point.
Contact with a car trips the runner rather than ending the run — three trips before capture — so hazard-kill is deliberately absent; the obstacles are obstacle-moving, not lethal regions.

The Karens are static blockers standing in lanes. They are filed as npc-population rather than a spawner, but they function as obstacles, and nothing in the option set expresses a person who is an obstacle.
P6 is genre-wide and not negotiable; spacing must be elastic against current speed rather than fixed studs.

notes_for_us: Infinite Runner has obstacle-jump and no counterpart for ducking, and duck-under obstacles are half of what the Subway Surfers vocabulary means. The option set covers one of the two verbs the prompt named.

The genre is defined as endless and this prompt gives the run a length and a destination. Nothing in the file says what to do with a finite runner; winner-zone came from Obby via the shared catalogue, and chunk rules and a fixed thirty-second course are not obviously compatible.
A person standing in the road as an obstacle has no home. npc-population is who lives here and spawner-npc is hostile emitters; a static human blocker is neither.
